And afterward she was reconciled with him,
and bore him sons and daughters.
And in that same year,
which is the year 1537 [of the Greeks],
623 of the Arabs [AH],
the Caliph al-Zahir died on the fourteenth of the seventh month,
having lived seventeen years.
This [caliph] began openly to ride out, to enter, and to go forth,
without being hidden from anyone.
And justice was revealed in him more than in his father;
and he began to distribute abundant alms,
and restored many buildings.
And he built this college {madrasa} which was named after him,
which had no equal in the world.
And he appointed in it four teachers for their four schools [of law],
and three hundred senior students,
for each student jurist rations {annonae} sufficient for him day by day.
And he built for them a private bath,
so that no stranger might enter it.
And he also appointed for them a private physician to treat their sick.
Concerning the decease of Chingiz
Khan.
And in the year 1524 [read: 1538 of the Greeks],
624 of the Arabs [AH], when Chingiz Khan returned from the lands of Khorasan to the east,
he set his mind to go and conquer the country of the Tanguts on the border of India.
And during his march a severe sickness overtook him from the bad air {OCR?} of that land.
And when he despaired of the help of physicians,
he sent and summoned his sons to him: Chagatai, that is, and Ogedei,
and Tolui,
and Kölgen,
and Jurchetei,
and Orda.
And he said to them:
"Behold, I am near to depart,
and by all means it is necessary to see a man
who is competent to preserve my kingdom without shaking.
And my will is this,
as I have told you at times,
that Ogedei sit on the throne of the kingdom in my place,
because I rely upon his wisdom and his orderly conduct.
Therefore, you my sons, what do you think?" Then all of them knelt on their knees and said:
"Our father and lord and king,
and we are all your servants,
and obedient to whatever you command us and direct."
And after this his sickness grew severe upon him,
and he departed from the world on the fourth of the ninth month, [Ramadan] of the fast of the Arabs, of that same year 624,
in August, 1538 [read: 1538 of the Greeks],
1227 of our Lord.
